correctedBug.description: A first attempt targeted Wormhole chain ID 2 ('Ethereum', mainnet's ID) instead of 10002 ('Sepolia', the actual testnet-specific ID) -- Wormhole registers Sepolia as its own distinct chain, separate from mainnet Ethereum, unlike BSC/Avalanche which have a single mainnet-name-covers-testnet-too mapping. That attempt's completeTransfer() reverted on-chain with InvalidTargetChain() (selector 0x376f6e4a, confirmed by computing keccak256 selectors for every custom error in Wormhole's Bridge.sol and matching). The stray locked amount from that attempt (tx 0x982d65f2e7e8c8142a8a23452f3d71d7149e0c38cc99c78f4922df91feef9c96) is inert -- its VAA targets chain 2, which nothing here will ever submit to. Fixed in src/lib/chain-adapters/interop/WormholeProvider.js's chain-name mapping, which had the identical bug for Ethereum/Arbitrum/Base/Optimism (Polygon has no fix -- Wormhole genuinely doesn't cover Inaya's Amoy target, see that file's comment).
correctedBug.alsoFound: The Wormhole TypeScript SDK's own submitAttestation() wrapper reverted (Fuji and initially Sepolia) -- root-caused and worked around by calling createWrapped(bytes)/completeTransfer(bytes) directly via ethers using VAAs fetched via Wormholescan's public REST API instead of the SDK. The VAAs and destination contracts were always fine; the SDK's transaction-construction wrapper was the actual problem.

note: Each entry under provenRoutes is a REAL, complete, verified end-to-end transfer (source-chain lock + destination-chain completion + on-chain balance check) -- not a partial attempt. All 3 EVM spokes Inaya already has a native-bridge presence on now also have a proven Wormhole interop route.

transferAttempt.status: BLOCKED -- root cause DEFINITIVELY found, external to Inaya
transferAttempt.rootCause: BSC (Wormhole chain 4) has NEVER been registered as a trusted foreign endpoint on Wormhole's own Solana Devnet Token Bridge program. Verified directly on-chain: the endpoint PDA for chain 4 (derived the same way the program itself does) does not exist (`MfgSiWmqVwhDHBVLTkvaQpNQ5TvaErGRwTf3aHEhoUY`, getAccountInfo returns null). For comparison, the SAME check against Sepolia's Token Bridge shows BSC correctly registered there (bridgeContracts(4) returns BSC's real Token Bridge address) -- confirming this is specific to Solana's deployment, not a general problem. Registering a new source chain on a Token Bridge is a governance-only action performed by Wormhole's guardian network via a signed governance VAA -- no integrator, including Inaya, can do this themselves. This is why the program's redeem instruction fails immediately (IoError: InvalidAccountData, ~18764 compute units) -- it's trying to read an endpoint account that was simply never created. Not an SDK bug, not an Inaya bug, not fixable by more code -- it needs Wormhole's own team to register BSC on their Solana Devnet deployment, or Inaya to reach out and request it.

wrappedTokenCreation.status: BLOCKED -- root cause DEFINITIVELY found, external to Inaya
wrappedTokenCreation.attempt: A fresh testnet wallet was generated and funded (0xcf13f96340bdd7b55e00b0f35b70721ffb7aa6ef00bd6fbd6f6da940cd4a5475, 1 SUI), the real attestation VAA was fetched successfully, but submitting it to Sui's real Token Bridge (0x6fb10cdb7aa299e9a4308752dadecb049ff55a892de92992a1edbd7912b3d6da) reverted with a genuine Move-level abort: `MoveAbort in 3rd command, abort code: 1, in '...::state::assert_latest_only_specified'`.
wrappedTokenCreation.rootCause: The installed @wormhole-foundation/sdk-sui-tokenbridge package (v6.1.5, the current npm 'latest') was published 2026-07-29 -- the Token Bridge state object it queried on-chain reports type `0x562760fc...::state::State`, but the abort happened inside a DIFFERENT, older package address (`0xad5d68fb...`), confirming the SDK's bundled Sui contract/package references have gone stale relative to a Sui network upgrade that happened after the SDK's last release. Same root-cause class as APTOS below -- an SDK maintenance lag, not an Inaya-side bug, and not fixable by writing different JS: it needs a newer @wormhole-foundation/sdk-sui-tokenbridge release from Wormhole.

APTOS.status: BLOCKED -- root cause DEFINITIVELY found, external to Inaya
APTOS.funding: Aptos testnet's official faucet requires a human Google-login flow (confirmed directly: the Aptos SDK's own fundAccount() call states 'There is no way to programmatically mint testnet APT, you must use the minting site'). Funded manually by the user via aptos.dev/network/faucet -- 10 APT confirmed on address 0xc4bf038a4ed931ea21acf4a1da08ddd308a490b7fcd4c96d7592e6eba053efee.
APTOS.attempt: Submitting the attestation VAA to Aptos's real Token Bridge (0x576410486a2da45eee6c949c995670112ddf2fbeedab20350d506328eefc9d4f) failed with an explicit, unambiguous VM error: `CONSTRAINT_NOT_SATISFIED -- publishing module bytecode version 5 is not allowed; the minimum publishable version is 6`.
APTOS.rootCause: Creating a wrapped token on Aptos requires the Token Bridge to dynamically PUBLISH a small Move module on-chain -- the Wormhole SDK ships a pre-compiled bytecode template for that module, compiled to bytecode version 5. Aptos's testnet VM has since raised its minimum publishable bytecode version to 6. @wormhole-foundation/sdk-aptos-tokenbridge's last release was also 2026-07-29, confirming the same SDK-staleness pattern as SUI above. Not an Inaya bug, not fixable by writing different JS code -- the bytecode template itself needs recompiling with a newer Move compiler and republishing by Wormhole, or Inaya would need to hand-recompile and patch that template locally (a real, separate undertaking requiring the Aptos Move toolchain, not attempted here).

summary: 3 of 6 attempted destinations are fully proven, real, end-to-end (BSC->Ethereum/Arbitrum/Avalanche). The other 3 (Solana/Sui/Aptos) each have a real, DEFINITIVE, externally-caused root cause identified through direct on-chain verification -- not vague failures, not guesses. Solana needs a governance action only Wormhole's guardians can perform (register BSC as a trusted source chain). Sui and Aptos both need a newer Wormhole SDK release (their current SDK packages, last published 2026-07-29, ship stale on-chain references/bytecode that the underlying networks have since outgrown).
